subject: C
topic: History of J&K — Historical Places & Importance

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Martand Sun Temple, one of the most magnificent ancient temples of Kashmir, was built during the reign of which dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Martand Sun Temple was built by King Lalitaditya Muktapida of the Karkota dynasty in the 8th century CE. It is dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and is located in Anantnag district. Lohara dynasty is wrong — they ruled from the 11th century onwards, after the temple was built. Utpala dynasty is wrong — they came after the Karkotas but before the Loharas. Shah Mir dynasty is wrong — they established the first Muslim rule in Kashmir in 1339 CE, centuries after the temple's construction.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Avantipur ruins:

(i) They were built by King Avantivarman of the Utpala dynasty.
(ii) The ruins include the Avantiswami Temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu.
(iii) The Avantisvara Temple at the site is dedicated to Lord Shiva.
(iv) Avantipur was established during the Mughal period in Kashmir.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — King Avantivarman (855–883 CE) of the Utpala dynasty founded Avantipur and built temples there. (ii) is correct — the Avantiswami Temple is dedicated to Lord Vishnu. (iii) is correct — the Avantisvara Temple at the site is dedicated to Lord Shiva. (iv) is wrong — Avantipur was established in the 9th century CE during the Utpala dynasty, not during the Mughal period which began in Kashmir in 1586 CE.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are historical forts located in the Jammu region?

(i) Akhnoor Fort
(ii) Bahu Fort
(iii) Hari Parbat Fort
(iv) Reasi Fort

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Akhnoor Fort is located in Akhnoor, Jammu district, on the banks of the Chenab river. (ii) is correct — Bahu Fort is located in Jammu city on the banks of the Tawi river. (iv) is correct — Reasi Fort (also called Bhimgarh Fort) is located in Reasi district of Jammu region. (iii) is wrong — Hari Parbat Fort is located in Srinagar, Kashmir valley, not in the Jammu region.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin is regarded as the greatest ruler of the medieval Kashmir.
Reason (R): He abolished the Jizya tax, promoted religious tolerance, and patronized art, architecture, and learning during his reign.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin (Budshah, r. 1420–1470) is widely regarded as the greatest ruler of medieval Kashmir. Reason (R) is also correct — he abolished the Jizya tax, promoted harmony between Hindus and Muslims, and patronized arts, crafts, and learning. (R) correctly explains (A) because his policies of tolerance and cultural patronage are the reasons he earned the title 'Budshah' (Great King). Option 2 is wrong because (R) directly explains why he is considered the greatest. Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Akhnoor Fort, situated on the banks of the Chenab River, was built by which ruler?
questions.explanation: Akhnoor Fort was originally built by Raja Tejh Singh in the 19th century. It is located on the right bank of the Chenab River in Akhnoor town. Maharaja Gulab Singh is wrong — he was the founder of the Dogra dynasty in J&K but did not build Akhnoor Fort. Raja Alam Singh is wrong — he was an earlier ruler of the region but not the builder of this fort. Maharaja Ranbir Singh is wrong — he was Gulab Singh's successor who focused on other constructions.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following historical places with their locations:

Column I:
(a) Martand Sun Temple
(b) Hari Parbat Fort
(c) Raghunath Temple
(d) Akhnoor Fort

Column II:
(i) Jammu city
(ii) Anantnag district
(iii) Srinagar
(iv) Akhnoor, Jammu

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Martand Sun Temple is located at Mattan in Anantnag district — matches (ii). (b) Hari Parbat Fort is located on Sharika hill in Srinagar — matches (iii). (c) Raghunath Temple is located in Jammu city — matches (i). (d) Akhnoor Fort is located in Akhnoor town, Jammu district — matches (iv). Option 1 wrongly places Martand in Srinagar. Option 2 wrongly swaps Raghunath Temple and Akhnoor Fort locations. Option 4 wrongly places Hari Parbat in Jammu.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Treaty of Amritsar was signed in __________, by which the British sold the territory of Kashmir to Maharaja Gulab Singh for 75 lakh Nanakshahi rupees.
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Amritsar was signed on 16 March 1846 between the British East India Company and Maharaja Gulab Singh. Under this treaty, the British transferred the Kashmir valley to Gulab Singh for 75 lakh Nanakshahi rupees. 1858 is wrong — that was the year the British Crown took over from the East India Company after the revolt of 1857. 1842 is wrong — that year saw the Treaty of Chushul between Tibet and the Dogras. 1839 is wrong — that was the year Maharaja Ranjit Singh of Punjab died.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Raghunath Temple in Jammu, one of the largest temple complexes in North India, was initiated by which Dogra ruler?
questions.explanation: The construction of Raghunath Temple in Jammu was initiated by Maharaja Gulab Singh in 1835 and completed by his son Maharaja Ranbir Singh in 1860. Since the temple was started and conceived by Gulab Singh, he is credited as its initiator. Maharaja Ranbir Singh is wrong as the initiator — though he completed it, the construction was started by Gulab Singh. Maharaja Hari Singh is wrong — he was the last Dogra ruler (1925–1947). Maharaja Pratap Singh is wrong — he ruled from 1885 to 1925.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the accession of J&K to India:

(i) Maharaja Hari Singh initially wanted J&K to remain independent.
(ii) The tribal invasion from Pakistan started on 22 October 1947.
(iii) The Instrument of Accession was signed on 26 October 1947.
(iv) Indian troops airlifted to Srinagar on 27 October 1947.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Maharaja Hari Singh initially wanted to remain independent and signed Standstill Agreements with both India and Pakistan. (ii) is correct — the tribal raiders backed by Pakistan invaded Kashmir on 22 October 1947. (iii) is correct — the Instrument of Accession was signed on 26 October 1947. (iv) is correct — Indian troops were airlifted to Srinagar airport on 27 October 1947 to defend the valley. All four statements are historically accurate.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Hari Parbat Fort in Srinagar is associated with both Mughal and Afghan periods of Kashmir's history.
Reason (R): The fort's wall was first built by Mughal Emperor Akbar, and the fort itself was later constructed by the Afghan Governor Atta Mohammad Khan.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Hari Parbat Fort is associated with both Mughal and Afghan periods. Reason (R) is also correct — the encircling wall was built by Mughal Emperor Akbar in 1590 CE, and the fort structure was later completed by Afghan Governor Atta Mohammad Khan in the 18th century. (R) explains (A) because it provides the specific historical evidence linking the fort to both periods. Option 1 is wrong because (R) directly explains why the fort is linked to both periods. Option 3 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (A) is also correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which Mughal Emperor ordered the construction of the Shalimar Bagh in Srinagar?
questions.explanation: Shalimar Bagh in Srinagar was laid out by Mughal Emperor Jahangir for his wife Empress Nur Jahan in 1619 CE. It is one of the finest Mughal gardens in Kashmir. Emperor Akbar is wrong — though he conquered Kashmir in 1586, Shalimar Bagh was built by his son Jahangir. Emperor Shah Jahan is wrong — he later extended the garden but was not its original creator. Emperor Aurangzeb is wrong — he was the last great Mughal emperor but did not build this garden.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Karkota dynasty of Kashmir:

(i) Durlabhvardhana was the founder of the Karkota dynasty.
(ii) Lalitaditya Muktapida was the most powerful king of this dynasty.
(iii) The Karkota dynasty ruled Kashmir from the 7th to the 9th century CE.
(iv) The capital of the Karkota dynasty was Parihasapura (modern Paraspore).

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Durlabhvardhana (c. 625–661 CE) founded the Karkota dynasty. (ii) is correct — Lalitaditya Muktapida (r. 724–760 CE) expanded the kingdom far beyond Kashmir and built the Martand Sun Temple. (iii) is correct — the Karkota dynasty ruled approximately from 625 CE to 855 CE. (iv) is correct — Lalitaditya built Parihasapura (modern Paraspore) as his capital near Srinagar. All four statements are historically accurate.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The famous Shankaracharya Temple on Takht-i-Sulaiman hill in Srinagar is believed to date back to which period?
questions.explanation: The Shankaracharya Temple (also known as Jyeshteswara Temple) on Takht-i-Sulaiman hill is believed to have been originally built around 200 BCE during the Mauryan period, making it one of the oldest temples in Kashmir. 8th century CE is wrong — though the temple was restored during the Karkota period, its origin is much earlier. 14th century CE is wrong — the Shah Mir dynasty established Muslim rule in Kashmir but did not build this temple. 16th century CE is wrong — the Mughals did not construct this temple.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly associated with Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin (Budshah)?

(i) He invited Hindu Pandits back to Kashmir who had left during Sikandar Butshikan's reign.
(ii) He introduced the art of papier-mâché in Kashmir.
(iii) He promoted shawl weaving and carpet making.
(iv) He built the Zaina Kadal bridge in Srinagar.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Zain-ul-Abidin invited the Hindu Pandits back who had fled during Sikandar Butshikan's persecution. (ii) is correct — he is credited with introducing papier-mâché art to Kashmir by bringing craftsmen from Central Asia. (iii) is correct — he promoted shawl weaving and carpet making, establishing these as key Kashmiri crafts. (iv) is correct — he constructed the Zaina Kadal (bridge) in Srinagar, which is named after him. All four statements are historically accurate.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Dogra dynasty's rule over Jammu and Kashmir began in which year with the Treaty of Amritsar?
questions.explanation: The Dogra dynasty's rule over Jammu and Kashmir formally began in 1846 with the Treaty of Amritsar, by which the British sold Kashmir to Maharaja Gulab Singh. 1820 is wrong — that year Gulab Singh became the Raja of Jammu under the Sikh Empire. 1857 is wrong — that was the year of the Indian Revolt against British rule. 1834 is wrong — in that year Gulab Singh's general Zorawar Singh conquered Ladakh.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following historical events with their correct years:

Column I:
(a) Accession of J&K to India
(b) Treaty of Amritsar
(c) Mughal conquest of Kashmir
(d) Establishment of Shah Mir dynasty

Column II:
(i) 1339 CE
(ii) 1586 CE
(iii) 1846 CE
(iv) 1947 CE

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Accession of J&K to India occurred in 1947 — matches (iv). (b) Treaty of Amritsar was signed in 1846 — matches (iii). (c) Mughal conquest of Kashmir by Akbar took place in 1586 — matches (ii). (d) Shah Mir established the first Muslim dynasty in Kashmir in 1339 — matches (i). Option 1 wrongly swaps years for Treaty of Amritsar and Mughal conquest. Option 3 wrongly assigns 1846 to accession. Option 4 wrongly swaps Mughal conquest and Shah Mir dynasty dates.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Sikandar Butshikan, the Sultan of Kashmir (1389–1413), is historically known for which of the following?
options: Building the Jama Masjid of Srinagar
Destruction of Hindu temples and forced conversions
questions.correctAnswer: Destruction of Hindu temples and forced conversions
questions.explanation: Sultan Sikandar (known as 'Butshikan' or Idol-Breaker) is historically known for his intolerant religious policies, including the destruction of Hindu temples and forced conversions. Building the Jama Masjid is wrong — it was built by Sultan Sikandar but he is remembered primarily as 'Butshikan'. Founding Anantnag is wrong — the city's history predates Sikandar. Establishing trade with China is wrong — this is not associated with his reign.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: In how many Nanakshahi rupees (in lakhs) was the territory of Kashmir sold to Maharaja Gulab Singh under the Treaty of Amritsar, 1846?
questions.explanation: Under the Treaty of Amritsar (1846), the British sold Kashmir to Maharaja Gulab Singh for 75 lakh Nanakshahi rupees (equivalent to Rs. 75,00,000). 50 lakhs is wrong — this is not the correct amount specified in the treaty. 60 lakhs is wrong — the treaty clearly mentions 75 lakhs. 85 lakhs is wrong — the amount was 75 lakhs, not 85 lakhs.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Lalitaditya Muktapida is considered the greatest king of ancient Kashmir.
Reason (R): He expanded the Karkota kingdom beyond Kashmir through military conquests and built magnificent temples including the Martand Sun Temple.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Lalitaditya Muktapida (r. 724–760 CE) is widely regarded as ancient Kashmir's greatest ruler. Reason (R) is also correct — he expanded his empire through conquests reaching Central Asia and built the magnificent Martand Sun Temple. (R) explains (A) because his military achievements and architectural patronage are the reasons he is considered the greatest. Option 1 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 2 is wrong because (A) is correct. Option 3 is wrong because (R) directly provides the reasons.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Pari Mahal (Palace of Fairies) in Srinagar was built by which Mughal prince?
questions.explanation: Pari Mahal was built by Mughal Prince Dara Shikoh, the eldest son of Emperor Shah Jahan, in the mid-17th century. It served as a library and school of astrology. Prince Aurangzeb is wrong — he was Dara Shikoh's brother and rival who later became emperor. Prince Shah Shuja is wrong — he was another son of Shah Jahan who governed Bengal. Prince Murad Baksh is wrong — he was the youngest son of Shah Jahan and did not build Pari Mahal.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Lohara dynasty of Kashmir:

(i) The Lohara dynasty was founded by Sangramaraja in 1003 CE.
(ii) The dynasty gets its name from the Lohara (Lohrin) region in the Pir Panjal range.
(iii) King Harsha of Kashmir belonged to this dynasty.
(iv) Kalhana, the author of Rajatarangini, wrote during the Lohara period.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Sangramaraja (r. 1003–1028 CE) founded the Lohara dynasty after the Utpala dynasty ended. (ii) is correct — the dynasty is named after Lohara (modern Lohrin) in the Pir Panjal mountains. (iii) is correct — King Harsha (r. 1089–1101 CE) was a notable and controversial Lohara king. (iv) is correct — Kalhana wrote Rajatarangini (River of Kings) in 1148–1150 CE during the reign of Lohara king Jayasimha. All statements are accurate.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Mughal Emperor __________ conquered Kashmir in 1586 CE, ending the rule of the Chak dynasty and incorporating Kashmir into the Mughal Empire.
questions.explanation: Mughal Emperor Akbar conquered Kashmir in 1586 CE by sending his general Qasim Khan, ending the rule of Yaqub Shah Chak, the last ruler of the Chak dynasty. Humayun is wrong — he ruled from 1530–1556 and did not conquer Kashmir. Babur is wrong — he founded the Mughal Empire in 1526 but never conquered Kashmir. Jahangir is wrong — he was Akbar's son who later visited Kashmir many times but the conquest was by his father.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The ancient Harwan archaeological site near Srinagar is significant because it contains remains from which period?
questions.explanation: The Harwan archaeological site near Srinagar contains remains from the Kushan period (1st–3rd century CE), including terracotta tiles depicting Buddhist scenes, indicating the spread of Buddhism in Kashmir during that era. Mughal period is wrong — the site predates Mughal rule by over a millennium. Sultanate period is wrong — the archaeological remains are from a much earlier period. Karkota period is wrong — the Harwan remains predate the Karkota dynasty by several centuries.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are features of the Dogra dynasty's rule in J&K?

(i) Construction of Raghunath Temple in Jammu
(ii) Establishment of Sri Pratap Singh Museum in Srinagar
(iii) Construction of Tawi Bridge in Jammu
(iv) Building of the Amar Mahal Palace

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Raghunath Temple was built by Maharaja Gulab Singh and completed by Maharaja Ranbir Singh. (ii) is correct — Sri Pratap Singh (SPS) Museum in Srinagar was established in 1898 during Maharaja Pratap Singh's reign. (iii) is correct — the Dogra rulers developed infrastructure including bridges over the Tawi River. (iv) is correct — Amar Mahal Palace in Jammu was built during the reign of Raja Amar Singh in the late 19th century. All are features of Dogra rule.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Burzahom archaeological site in Kashmir, known for Neolithic remains, is located near which city?
questions.explanation: Burzahom is an important Neolithic archaeological site located about 16 km from Srinagar. It provides evidence of the earliest known human habitation in Kashmir dating to around 3000 BCE. Anantnag is wrong — Burzahom is not in Anantnag district. Baramulla is wrong — the site is not located near Baramulla. Pulwama is wrong — while relatively close, Burzahom is administratively and geographically identified with the Srinagar area.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession to India on 26 October 1947.
Reason (R): Pakistani tribal raiders had invaded Kashmir, forcing the Maharaja to seek Indian military assistance.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947. Reason (R) is also correct — Pakistani tribal raiders invaded Kashmir on 22 October 1947, threatening Srinagar. (R) explains (A) because the tribal invasion forced the Maharaja to seek Indian military help, which was conditional upon accession. Option 1 is wrong because (R) is historically accurate. Option 2 is wrong because (R) directly explains the reason for accession. Option 3 is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following Dogra rulers with their major contributions:

Column I:
(a) Maharaja Gulab Singh
(b) Maharaja Ranbir Singh
(c) Maharaja Pratap Singh
(d) Maharaja Hari Singh

Column II:
(i) Established the first state council and introduced modern reforms
(ii) Founded the Dogra dynasty's rule over J&K
(iii) Completed the Raghunath Temple and promoted Sanskrit learning
(iv) Signed the Instrument of Accession to India

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Maharaja Gulab Singh founded the Dogra dynasty's rule over J&K through the Treaty of Amritsar (1846) — matches (ii). (b) Maharaja Ranbir Singh completed the Raghunath Temple and was a great patron of Sanskrit learning — matches (iii). (c) Maharaja Pratap Singh established the first state council and brought modern administrative reforms — matches (i). (d) Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession in 1947 — matches (iv). Option 1 swaps (b) and (c). Option 3 wrongly assigns temple to Gulab Singh. Option 4 wrongly assigns accession to Pratap Singh.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Jama Masjid of Srinagar, one of the oldest mosques in Kashmir, was originally built during the reign of which Sultan?
questions.explanation: The Jama Masjid of Srinagar was originally built by Sultan Sikandar in 1394 CE. It can accommodate over 33,000 worshippers. Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin is wrong — though he renovated many structures, the original Jama Masjid was built by his father Sikandar. Shah Mir is wrong — he established the first Muslim dynasty in Kashmir but the mosque was built later. Sultan Qutb-ud-din is wrong — he preceded Sikandar but did not build this mosque.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Study the following timeline of major dynasties that ruled Kashmir:

Karkota → 625–855 CE, 230 years
Utpala → 855–1003 CE, 148 years
Lohara → 1003–1339 CE, 336 years
Shah Mir → 1339–1561 CE, 222 years

Which dynasty ruled Kashmir for the longest period?
questions.explanation: From the table, the Lohara dynasty ruled for approximately 336 years (1003–1339 CE), which is the longest duration. Karkota dynasty is wrong — they ruled for about 230 years, which is less than the Lohara dynasty. Shah Mir dynasty is wrong — they ruled for about 222 years. Utpala dynasty is wrong — they had the shortest reign at approximately 148 years.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The ancient Pandrethan Temple (Pandrathan) near Srinagar was built during the reign of which king?
options: King Lalitaditya of the Karkota dynasty
King Avantivarman of the Utpala dynasty
King Partha (Pandrathan) of the Utpala dynasty
questions.correctAnswer: King Partha (Pandrathan) of the Utpala dynasty
questions.explanation: The Pandrethan Temple was built during the reign of King Partha (r. 921–931 CE) of the Utpala dynasty. The town Pandrethan (ancient Puranadhisthana) is named after him. King Lalitaditya is wrong — he was a Karkota ruler who built Martand Temple. King Avantivarman is wrong — though he was from the same Utpala dynasty, the Pandrethan Temple is attributed to King Partha. Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin is wrong — he was a medieval Muslim ruler.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Mughal rule in Kashmir:

(i) Kashmir was conquered by Akbar in 1586 CE.
(ii) The Mughals built famous gardens like Nishat Bagh and Shalimar Bagh.
(iii) Mughal rule in Kashmir lasted for about 167 years.
(iv) The last Mughal governor of Kashmir was defeated by the Afghans in 1753 CE.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Akbar conquered Kashmir in 1586 CE through his general Qasim Khan. (ii) is correct — Nishat Bagh was built by Asaf Khan (1633) and Shalimar Bagh by Emperor Jahangir (1619). (iii) is correct — Mughal rule lasted from 1586 to 1753 CE, approximately 167 years. (iv) is correct — the Afghan commander Ahmad Shah Durrani's forces defeated the Mughals in Kashmir in 1753 CE. All four statements are historically accurate.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Which ruler is credited with the construction of the fort wall around Hari Parbat hill in Srinagar?
questions.explanation: Mughal Emperor Akbar ordered the construction of the fort wall (encircling wall) around Hari Parbat hill in 1590 CE. The actual fort structure was later built by Afghan Governor Atta Mohammad Khan. Afghan Governor Atta Mohammad Khan is wrong for the wall — he built the fort on top but not the encircling wall. Dogra Maharaja Gulab Singh is wrong — the wall predates Dogra rule. Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin is wrong — the wall was built over a century after his reign.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Study the following data about important historical sites of J&K:

Martand Sun Temple → Lalitaditya Muktapida, 8th century CE
Raghunath Temple → Maharaja Gulab Singh, 19th century CE
Hari Parbat Fort Wall → Emperor Akbar, 16th century CE
Pari Mahal → Prince Dara Shikoh, 17th century CE

Which historical site among those listed above is the oldest?
questions.explanation: From the data table, the Martand Sun Temple was built in the 8th century CE, making it the oldest among the listed sites. Hari Parbat Fort Wall is wrong — it was built in the 16th century CE, eight centuries after Martand. Raghunath Temple is wrong — it was built in the 19th century, the most recent. Pari Mahal is wrong — it was built in the 17th century CE.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Nishat Bagh in Srinagar, known as the 'Garden of Joy', was designed by which Mughal noble?
questions.explanation: Nishat Bagh was designed and built by Asaf Khan (brother of Empress Nur Jahan and father-in-law of Emperor Shah Jahan) in 1633 CE. It is located on the eastern shore of Dal Lake. Mir Sayyid Ali Hamdani is wrong — he was a 14th-century Sufi saint from Persia. Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan is wrong — he was a Mughal poet and minister but not associated with this garden. Raja Man Singh is wrong — he was a Mughal general but did not design Nishat Bagh.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are historical monuments associated with Mughal rule in Kashmir?

(i) Shalimar Bagh
(ii) Nishat Bagh
(iii) Pari Mahal
(iv) Martand Sun Temple

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Shalimar Bagh was built by Mughal Emperor Jahangir in 1619 CE. (ii) is correct — Nishat Bagh was built by Mughal noble Asaf Khan in 1633 CE. (iii) is correct — Pari Mahal was built by Mughal Prince Dara Shikoh in the mid-17th century. (iv) is wrong — Martand Sun Temple was built by Karkota king Lalitaditya in the 8th century CE, centuries before Mughal rule. Therefore, (i), (ii) and (iii) only is the correct answer.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: Maharaja Ranbir Singh of Jammu and Kashmir is particularly remembered for his contribution to which field?
options: Construction of modern railways in J&K
Establishing the first printing press in Kashmir
Promotion of Sanskrit learning and literature
questions.correctAnswer: Promotion of Sanskrit learning and literature
questions.explanation: Maharaja Ranbir Singh (r. 1856–1885) is remembered for his patronage of Sanskrit learning and literature. He established the Raghunath Temple library, commissioned translations of Sanskrit texts, and promoted Oriental studies. Construction of railways is wrong — railways in J&K came much later. Western medical education is wrong — this is not his primary contribution. Establishing a printing press is wrong — though publishing grew during his time, his main legacy is Sanskrit scholarship.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following Sultans of Kashmir with their contributions:

Column I:
(a) Shah Mir
(b) Sultan Sikandar
(c) Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin
(d) Yusuf Shah Chak

Column II:
(i) Last independent ruler before Mughal conquest
(ii) Founded the first Muslim dynasty in Kashmir
(iii) Known as 'Budshah' for religious tolerance
(iv) Known as 'Butshikan' (Idol-Breaker)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Shah Mir founded the first Muslim dynasty (Shah Mir dynasty) in Kashmir in 1339 CE — matches (ii). (b) Sultan Sikandar is known as 'Butshikan' (Idol-Breaker) for destroying Hindu temples — matches (iv). (c) Sultan Zain-ul-Abidin is known as 'Budshah' (Great King) for his religious tolerance — matches (iii). (d) Yusuf Shah Chak was the last independent ruler of Kashmir before Mughal conquest in 1586 — matches (i). Option 1 swaps (b) and (c). Option 2 swaps (a) and (d). Option 3 swaps (c) and (d).

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Bahu Fort in Jammu:

(i) It is believed to have been built by Raja Bahulochan over 3000 years ago.
(ii) The fort is located on the left bank of the Tawi River.
(iii) A temple dedicated to Goddess Kali (Bave Wali Mata) is located inside the fort.
(iv) The fort was rebuilt by the Dogra rulers in the 19th century.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — tradition attributes the fort's construction to Raja Bahulochan, believed to be over 3000 years old. (ii) is correct — Bahu Fort is situated on the left bank of the Tawi River in Jammu. (iii) is correct — the fort houses the ancient temple of Bave Wali Mata (Goddess Kali). (iv) is correct — the Dogra rulers, particularly in the 19th century, rebuilt and renovated the fort. All four statements are correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Afghan rule over Kashmir (1753–1819) is historically characterized by which of the following?
options: Expansion of trade with Central Asia
questions.explanation: The Afghan rule over Kashmir (1753–1819) is historically characterized by oppressive governance, heavy taxation, and exploitation of the local population. The Afghan governors were known for their harsh policies. Great architectural development is wrong — the Afghan period saw neglect rather than construction. Religious tolerance is wrong — the period was marked by intolerance. Expansion of trade with Central Asia is wrong — the Afghan period disrupted rather than expanded trade.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: In which year was the Rajatarangini (River of Kings), the historical chronicle of Kashmir, composed by Kalhana?
questions.explanation: Kalhana composed the Rajatarangini in 1148–1150 CE during the reign of Lohara king Jayasimha. It is the earliest known historical work of Kashmir, chronicling the history of Kashmir's kings from earliest times. 1250 CE is wrong — the work was completed a century earlier. 1050 CE is wrong — this predates Kalhana's lifetime. 1320 CE is wrong — this is nearly two centuries after the actual composition.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Burzahom archaeological site is one of the most important prehistoric sites in the Indian subcontinent.
Reason (R): Burzahom provides evidence of Neolithic, Megalithic, and early historical periods of human habitation in Kashmir.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — Burzahom is recognized as one of the most significant prehistoric sites in the Indian subcontinent. Reason (R) is also correct — excavations have revealed evidence of Neolithic (c. 3000 BCE), Megalithic, and early historical phases. (R) explains (A) because the multi-period evidence is what makes the site important. Option 1 is wrong because (A) is correct. Option 2 is wrong because (R) is archaeologically accurate. Option 4 is wrong because (R) directly explains why the site is important.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Sikh rule over Kashmir (1819–1846) began when which Sikh commander conquered the region?
questions.explanation: The Sikh conquest of Kashmir in 1819 was led by Misr Diwan Chand under the orders of Maharaja Ranjit Singh, ending the Afghan rule. Ranjit Dev is wrong — he was a Dogra chief of Jammu in the 18th century. Hari Singh Nalwa is wrong — he was a famous Sikh general but his campaigns were in the North-West Frontier, not Kashmir. Wazir Zorawar Singh is wrong — he was a Dogra general who conquered Ladakh in 1834 under Gulab Singh.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are correctly paired regarding historical places and their significance?

(i) Burzahom — Neolithic site with pit dwellings
(ii) Harwan — Kushan period Buddhist tiles
(iii) Akhnoor Fort — Mughal architecture
(iv) Avantipur — Utpala dynasty temples

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Burzahom is a Neolithic site known for pit dwellings dating to around 3000 BCE. (ii) is correct — Harwan has terracotta tiles from the Kushan period depicting Buddhist motifs. (iv) is correct — Avantipur has temples built by Utpala dynasty king Avantivarman. (iii) is wrong — Akhnoor Fort is associated with Dogra period architecture (built by Raja Tejh Singh), not Mughal architecture. Therefore, (i), (ii) and (iv) only is correct.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Study the following information about rulers and their historical contributions to J&K:

Maharaja Gulab Singh → 1846–1857, Founded Dogra rule, initiated Raghunath Temple
Maharaja Ranbir Singh → 1857–1885, Completed Raghunath Temple, promoted Sanskrit
Maharaja Pratap Singh → 1885–1925, Established SPS Museum, administrative reforms
Maharaja Hari Singh → 1925–1947, Accession to India, introduced free education

Which Dogra ruler had the longest reign based on the data above?
questions.explanation: From the table: Maharaja Gulab Singh ruled for 11 years (1846–1857), Maharaja Ranbir Singh ruled for 28 years (1857–1885), Maharaja Pratap Singh ruled for 40 years (1885–1925), and Maharaja Hari Singh ruled for 22 years (1925–1947). Therefore, Maharaja Pratap Singh had the longest reign at 40 years. Maharaja Ranbir Singh is wrong — he ruled for 28 years. Maharaja Hari Singh is wrong — he ruled for 22 years. Maharaja Gulab Singh is wrong — he had the shortest reign at 11 years.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Maharaja Gulab Singh:

(i) He was originally a feudatory of the Sikh Empire under Maharaja Ranjit Singh.
(ii) He acquired Kashmir through the Treaty of Amritsar in 1846.
(iii) He initiated the construction of Raghunath Temple in Jammu.
(iv) He conquered Tibet and established trade relations with China.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Gulab Singh served as a feudal lord under Maharaja Ranjit Singh of the Sikh Empire and was made Raja of Jammu. (ii) is correct — through the Treaty of Amritsar (1846), he acquired Kashmir from the British for 75 lakh rupees. (iii) is correct — he initiated the construction of Raghunath Temple in 1835. (iv) is wrong — while his general Zorawar Singh invaded western Tibet (Ladakh), it was not a successful conquest of Tibet proper and he did not establish formal trade with China.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Chashme Shahi garden in Srinagar was built during the reign of which Mughal Emperor?
questions.explanation: Chashme Shahi (Royal Spring) was built in 1632 CE during the reign of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan by his governor Ali Mardan Khan. It is the smallest of the three Mughal gardens in Srinagar. Jahangir is wrong — though he built Shalimar Bagh, Chashme Shahi was built during his son's reign. Akbar is wrong — he conquered Kashmir but this garden was built later. Aurangzeb is wrong — the garden was built before his reign.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Shah Hamadan Mosque (Khanqah-e-Moula) in Srinagar is named after which Sufi saint?
questions.explanation: Khanqah-e-Moula (Shah Hamadan Mosque) is named after Mir Sayyid Ali Hamdani, a Persian Sufi saint who visited Kashmir in the 14th century and played a significant role in the spread of Islam in the valley. Sheikh Noor-ud-Din Noorani is wrong — he is known as Nund Rishi and has his own shrine at Charar-i-Sharief. Bulbul Shah is wrong — he was the first Muslim missionary in Kashmir but this mosque is not named after him. Shah-i-Hamadan Qadri is wrong — this is not a real historical figure.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText: The Mubarak Mandi Palace complex in Jammu was the royal residence of which rulers?
questions.explanation: The Mubarak Mandi Palace complex in Jammu served as the royal residence of the Dogra rulers from the 19th century until 1925, when Maharaja Hari Singh moved to Hari Niwas Palace. Mughal governors is wrong — the Mughal governors were based in Srinagar, not Jammu. Afghan rulers is wrong — they did not build this palace. Sikh governors is wrong — the Mubarak Mandi complex was built and used by the Dogra dynasty.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Match the following historical periods with their correct sequence in Kashmir:

Column I:
(a) Afghan rule
(b) Sikh rule
(c) Mughal rule
(d) Dogra rule

Column II:
(i) 1586–1753 CE
(ii) 1753–1819 CE
(iii) 1819–1846 CE
(iv) 1846–1947 CE

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: (a) Afghan rule lasted from 1753–1819 CE — matches (ii). (b) Sikh rule lasted from 1819–1846 CE — matches (iii). (c) Mughal rule lasted from 1586–1753 CE — matches (i). (d) Dogra rule lasted from 1846–1947 CE — matches (iv). The chronological sequence is: Mughal → Afghan → Sikh → Dogra. Option 1 wrongly assigns Mughal period to Afghan rule. Option 2 swaps Sikh and Dogra periods. Option 3 swaps Afghan and Sikh periods.

questions.subject: C
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Chak dynasty of Kashmir:

(i) The Chak dynasty was the last independent Muslim dynasty of Kashmir.
(ii) Yusuf Shah Chak was the last ruler of this dynasty.
(iii) The Chaks were originally from the Dardic tribe of Gilgit.
(iv) The Chak dynasty was overthrown by the Mughal Emperor Akbar in 1586 CE.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Chak dynasty (1561–1586 CE) was the last independent Muslim dynasty to rule Kashmir before Mughal annexation. (ii) is correct — Yusuf Shah Chak was the last ruler of the Chak dynasty who was defeated by the Mughals. (iii) is correct — the Chaks were originally from a Dardic tribe that migrated from the Gilgit region. (iv) is correct — Mughal Emperor Akbar overthrew the Chak dynasty in 1586 CE through his general Qasim Khan. All four statements are historically accurate.
